sections.html:
Pittsfield is the largest city and the county seat of Berkshire County in western Massachusetts. It is 48 miles northwest of Springfield, 135 miles west of Boston and 39 miles east of Albany, New York. The 2020 census counted 43,927 residents, and the population has declined in recent decades from a peak above 50,000 in 1930.

The city covers 42.46 square miles, 2.00 of them water, at an elevation of about 1,040 feet. Lanesborough lies to the north, Dalton to the east, Washington to the southeast, Lenox to the south, Richmond to the southwest and Hancock to the west. Most residents live on roughly a quarter of the land, and the west side holds the 11,000-acre Pittsfield State Forest. The east and west branches of the Housatonic River meet here, between the Berkshire Hills and the Taconic Range.

sections.h2: The GE cleanup and your address
sections.html:
PCBs from the former General Electric plant contaminated the Housatonic River and its floodplain, and the area is a federal Superfund site. EPA added it to the Superfund list in September 1997. A settlement valued at over $250 million was reached in 1999 and entered as a consent decree the next year.

Between 2005 and 2018, GE finished remediation and restoration of the ten plant areas within the city, and it continues monitoring and maintenance. Downstream cleanup was still unfinished as of 2025.

  • The site includes the plant area, river banks, floodplains, filled former oxbows and Allendale School.
  • If your house is near the river or a former plant area, ask your attorney what is on record for the address.
  • A direct buyer can price the question in rather than asking you to resolve it first.

Most houses in the city are not affected, so do not assume the worst, but do find out before a buyer's attorney asks.

Pittsfield has a humid continental climate, and its elevation makes the winters harsh.

Heating cost, roof condition and pipe protection count for more here than in a milder place. A house left empty through a winter may have freeze damage, and both lenders and buyers' inspectors look for it. If you are managing a vacant or inherited property, check the pipes and the roof before the first hard freeze.

U.S. Route 7 and U.S. Route 20 cross in Pittsfield. Route 8 passes through the northeast corner, joined in part with Route 9, and Route 41 starts in the southwest. The nearest interstate is I-90, the Massachusetts Turnpike, about 10 miles south in Lee.

The Joseph Scelsi Intermodal Transportation Center handles Amtrak trains and Peter Pan buses and serves as the hub of the Berkshire Regional Transit Authority. Pittsfield Municipal Airport takes private and charter flights, and Albany International is the nearest airport with national service.

Onota Lake and Pontoosuc Lake feed the west branch of the Housatonic, and Pontoosuc lies partly in Lanesborough. Houses near those shores and near the river sit in different conditions from hillside homes, and a seller should know whether the property is close to water.

  • Wahconah Park is a local baseball landmark.
  • The Berkshire Museum and Berkshire Athenaeum are downtown.
  • Pittsfield State Forest offers hiking, camping and swimming.

Berkshire Medical Center and Berkshire Community College are in the city, and about 6,000 students attend its public schools. Pittsfield sets its tax rates and bill dates locally, so call the assessor or treasurer for current figures.

Massachusetts requires a fire department certificate to sell a home. Phone the local fire department once a closing date is set, and expect a fee. An alarm with no manufacture date counts as expired. Details are on the Mass.gov alarm inspection page.

Attorneys take part in Massachusetts sales by law and by practice, and most deeds are filed as recorded land at the registry of deeds. The deed excise in Chapter 64D, Section 1 counts the sale price without liens that stay on the property.

Under 760 CMR 74, sellers of certain residential properties may not condition an offer on a waiver of the home inspection.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or vacant house
sections.html:
Heirs selling a Pittsfield house need to show estate paperwork before a deed can transfer, and an attorney can tell you which documents your situation needs. Plan for that early, since it often takes longer than the fire certificate or the tax check.

Collect the deed, the most recent tax information from the city, notes about the heating system and roof, and anything you know about the river or plant areas if your property is near them. Walk through the house once to check for winter damage. If anyone lives far away, name one person to deal with the attorney so the paperwork moves in one direction.

sections.h2: Older houses from a manufacturing city
sections.html:
Pittsfield was incorporated as a town in 1761 and as a city in 1891. Woolen manufacturing dominated for almost a century, and William Stanley Jr. produced the first electric transformer here after moving his company in 1891. General Electric bought that firm in 1903. GE later cut its workforce from over 13,000 to a small number, and General Dynamics now occupies many of the old GE buildings.

That history left a mix of worker housing, older homes near the downtown and houses set on hillsides. Age shows up in heating systems, wiring and roofs, so expect an inspector to look hard at those items before a buyer commits.

sections.h2: What a seller does, in order
sections.html:
The steps are the same for a listing and a cash sale, and the order below saves time.

  • Decide on a closing date, even a rough one, and call the fire department about the alarm certificate.
  • Replace any alarm that is expired or has no manufacture date.
  • Ask the assessor or treasurer about the current tax situation on the property.
  • Give your attorney the deed, any payoff figures and estate paperwork if it applies.
  • Sign the deed at closing and make sure it is recorded at the registry of deeds.

An owner who starts with the paperwork instead of the repairs usually reaches a closing sooner, because the paperwork is what holds up a deed.

sections.h2: When a direct sale suits an owner
sections.html:
A direct sale can suit owners of older houses, inherited property and homes that need heating or roof work.

  • Estates with heirs living elsewhere.
  • Houses left vacant through a winter.
  • Owners who need a set closing date.

Tell us the address, who is on the deed and any debts against the property, and we can explain how a sale would be handled. The same Massachusetts steps apply to a direct purchase: an attorney, the fire department certificate, payoff of any mortgage or lien and a recorded deed.

faqs.a: Yes. Pittsfield is the most populous city and the county seat of Berkshire County.

faqs.q: How much snow does Pittsfield get?
faqs.a: Average annual snowfall is about 73 inches, and temperatures reach 0 degrees or colder 13 times a year.

faqs.q: Does the GE cleanup affect every Pittsfield house?
faqs.a: No. The Superfund site covers the plant area, the river, its banks and floodplains, and other named areas. Ask your attorney what is on record for your address.

faqs.q: Do I need a fire department certificate to sell in Pittsfield?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale or transfer requires a certificate of compliance showing your alarms meet state requirements.

faqs.q: Where do I find Pittsfield's current tax rate?
faqs.a: Ask the city assessor or treasurer.
